judgements.reason: Counting the unnumbered title page (PDF p. 1), the seven numbered body pages (PDF pp. 2-8), and the non-reference 'Code and Data' and 'Author Contributions' sections on PDF p. 9 places non-reference, non-appendix content at nine physical pages against an eight-page cap.

On the title page (PDF p. 1), '\authorcell{Alejandro Castellanos}{}' leaves the first author's affiliation blank and 'With Apart Research' does not clarify whether Apart Research is an affiliation, sponsor, or organizer.

The manuscript refers to a '2026-11-09' audit and correction (PDF p. 9, 'Code and Data' and 'Author Contributions'; PDF p. 15, 'LLM Usage Statement') without stating submission timestamps or timezones relative to the November 8, 11:59 PM AoE deadline.

In Section 3.1 and Section 3.4 (PDF pp. 3-4), the 12 target invalid cases (build-only, wrong-artifact, wrong-run) are deterministic field mismatches that are mechanically decidable, and the paper provides no worked example contrasting receipt inspection with attestation binding.

Contribution 5 (PDF p. 2) claims 'complete logs', whereas Appendix D (PDF p. 15) explicitly states that retained records store parsed outcomes, reasons, and short prompt hashes rather than full prompts, raw responses, executable git revisions, or retry arrays.

Section 3.4 (PDF p. 5) states unconditionally that 'caps are kept non-binding by retrying truncated responses at larger caps', while Appendices B.3, C.3, and D (PDF pp. 12-15) acknowledge that 30,096 of 32,832 main records lack retry metadata and that replacing the truncated DeepSeek 30% run changed 4-of-7 hidden capture from 1 to 0.

Phrases such as 'We explore every reachable state of the real kernel' in Section 3.2 (PDF p. 4), 'The guarantee also assumes... independent honest errors' in Section 5 (PDF p. 8), and 'defeats the bound' in Appendix A (PDF p. 11) blur the boundaries between bounded mechanical check G1, seat bound G2, and probabilistic model G3.

In Section 3.2 (PDF p. 4), invariant S2 ('an eligible execution attempt succeeds') verifies immediate step-level execution success rather than temporal liveness under fairness assumptions, while Finding 3 (PDF p. 6) uses 'liveness' to refer to valid-release acceptance.

Finding 2 (PDF p. 6) claims the 4-of-7 committee 'matched the gated majority's safety at 10%' based on zero captures across only 12 independent draws, and Section 3.4 (PDF p. 5) omits the selection rule used to derive 1, 3, and 5 seats from the 7-seat committee draw.

Table 1's caption (PDF p. 6) states that outcomes are pooled over colluder shares 10-50% (which yields the 120 target trials), but the 96 valid and 48 forged trials actually pool across all six shares 0-50% (6 shares x 2 conditions x 8 valid or 4 forged cases).

Figure 1's caption (PDF p. 7) claims to show 'the committee regimes that were ever captured', but omits Committee 3-of-5 (which had 23 DS and 20 GPT captures in Table 1) and plots only the theoretical G3 curve without the realized G2 seat bound.

The paper cites arXiv:2603.25100 by a title fragment ('From Logic Monopoly, 2026') on PDF pp. 2, 3, and 9 instead of author names, leaves SQLite yearless, and omits volume/page numbers for several classic references on PDF pp. 9-10.

Table 1 (PDF p. 6), Figure 1 (PDF p. 7), and Figure 2/Table 4 (PDF p. 14) are placed mid-sentence, splitting prose across page boundaries, and PDF p. 10 is mostly blank after the final five references.

Acronyms such as MCP, A2A, HMAC, and TF-IDF appear without expansion on PDF pp. 2, 3, and 5, and the distinction between receipt, evidence, proposal, and attestation in Section 3.1 (PDF p. 3) is compressed without a worked example.

Colloquialisms such as 'implements nothing, measures nothing', 'two things no constitution allows', and 'the checker has teeth' on PDF p. 2, as well as 'buys safety with liveness' for availability on PDF p. 6, are unnecessarily rhetorical.

Section 3.4 (PDF p. 5) notes that visible-board auditors see the 50-agent vote tally and recent comments before attesting, yet Table 1 and Finding 2 (PDF p. 6) pool visible-board and hidden-board runs when discussing standalone 7-request committees.

Section 3.4 (PDF p. 5) and Appendix D (PDF p. 15) disclose that the gated-majority control uses fresh synthetic receipts and keys offline, so explicitly stating which case fields, vote totals, and kernel checks are preserved strengthens Finding 1.
Section 4.3 (PDF p. 7) reports a detector F1 range of 0.97-1.0 without providing per-share precision, recall, TP/FP/FN counts, or threshold sensitivity in Appendix B.4 (PDF p. 13).

Section 4.1 (PDF p. 5) states that all seven mutants had shortest counterexamples of four to six actions, whereas Table 2 (PDF p. 12) omits explicit action step counts for the seat, binding, duplicate, and audit mutants.

As reported in Section 4.3 (PDF p. 7), honest auditor error on the main exact-match receipt task is 0/746 per model, leaving the correlated honest-error independence assumption of G3 empirically untested.

Section 3.4 (PDF p. 5), Finding 1 (PDF p. 6), and Appendix D (PDF p. 15) confirm that direct-majority forgery approval (48/48) holds by construction because voters lack the symmetric HMAC key, and that the gated-majority control is reconstructed offline with fresh synthetic keys.

Table 1's footnote (PDF p. 6) notes that the 120 pooled target trials come from only 60 independent committee draws (12 per share) shared across board conditions and models, so small count differences between regimes and models reflect paired draw noise.
The title page (PDF p. 1) leaves Alejandro Castellanos's affiliation empty while listing University of Toronto for Ignatius Pio Binawan.
On PDF pp. 9-10, SQLite lacks a year, arXiv:2603.25100 is cited by title fragment, author lists mix 'et al.' with full lists, and several 2026 arXiv identifiers merit source verification.

In Figure 1 (PDF p. 7), the three subplots are compact with small markers, and Table 1 (PDF p. 6) buries the essential '60 independent committee draws, not 120' design caveat in a dense footnote rather than the main caption or column header.

Section 4.3 (PDF p. 7) summarizes public-log collusion detection as 'F1 of 0.97-1.0 at every share' in a single paragraph without providing a per-share precision/recall/F1 table in Appendix B.4 or Appendix C.

Historical manifests lack git commit hashes, pinned temperature, prompt versions, and provider request IDs, and event records omit full prompts and raw responses, a limitation currently deferred to Appendix A (PDF p. 11) and Appendix D (PDF p. 15) rather than stated in Section 3.4.

Counting the unnumbered title page (PDF p. 1), the seven numbered body pages (PDF pp. 2-8), and the non-reference 'Code and Data' and 'Author Contributions' sections on PDF p. 9 makes compliance with the 8-page non-reference limit ambiguous.
Table 1's caption (PDF p. 6) claims pooling over colluder shares 10-50%, which matches the 120 target trials, whereas the 96 valid and 48 forged trials include the 0% colluder share.

Figure 1 (PDF p. 7) and Table 3 (PDF p. 13) omit the captured Committee 3-of-5 regime (23 DS and 20 GPT captures in Table 1) and omit the per-share realized G2 seat bounds that explain the non-monotonic dip at 40% collusion.

Section 3.4 (PDF p. 5) never specifies how the 1-of-1, 2-of-3, and 3-of-5 committees are derived from the 7-seat draw, and Table 1/Figure 1 pool visible-board runs (where auditors see the 50-agent vote tally) with hidden-board runs.

Section 3.4 (PDF p. 5) claims caps are kept non-binding via retries, whereas Appendices B.3, C.3, and D (PDF pp. 12-15) show that 30,096 of 32,832 main records lack retry metadata and that replacing the truncated DeepSeek 30% run changed 4-of-7 hidden capture from 1 to 0.

Contribution 5 (PDF p. 2) overstates 'complete logs' relative to Appendix D (PDF p. 15), S2 in Section 3.2 (PDF p. 4) is step-level execution success rather than temporal liveness, and several global phrases blur G1, G2, and G3.

Appendices B.2 and C.2 (PDF pp. 12-13) consist of two-word fragments ('Table 2.' and 'Table 4.'), appendix heading styles vary, Table 2 omits step counts for several mutants, and PDF p. 10 is mostly blank.

Because the unnumbered title page (PDF p. 1) is followed by seven numbered pages (PDF pp. 2-8) plus 'Code and Data' and 'Author Contributions' on PDF p. 9, moving those two meta-sections to an appendix avoids any violation of the 8-page main-body cap.
The first author's affiliation argument in '\authorcell{Alejandro Castellanos}{}' on PDF p. 1 is empty, and 'With Apart Research' is ambiguous.
The bibliography (PDF pp. 9-10) formats 'From Logic Monopoly (2026)' without authors, leaves 'SQLite()' without a year, and alternates between literal 'et al.' and full author lists.

Section 3.4 (PDF p. 5) and Appendix D (PDF p. 15) explain that the gated-majority control uses fresh synthetic receipts and keys offline because original signing keys were not retained, warranting a clear equivalence explanation in Section 3.4.

In Section 3.4 (PDF p. 5), the sentence 'Non-reasoning models were excluded so that reasoning mode would not be confounded with family' is awkwardly phrased when the design simply holds reasoning mode constant across two model families.

Table 1 (PDF p. 6) pools 120 paired target trials from 60 independent draws and Figure 1 (PDF p. 7) plots n=24 paired trials (12 independent draws) per point without showing the realized G2 seat bound or draw-level uncertainty.

Appendices B and C (PDF pp. 12-13) use bold run-in '\head{B.1 ...}' paragraphs instead of '\subsection', B.2 and C.2 are two-word fragments, and Table 2 (PDF p. 12) omits explicit shortest-counterexample step counts for several mutants.
PDF p. 10 (numbered page 9) contains only the final five bibliography entries at the top and is otherwise blank due to the '\clearpage' before Appendix A.

Section 4.3 (PDF p. 7), Appendix A (PDF p. 11), and Table 4 (PDF p. 14) switch between denominators (0/746 target seats, 2/108 case-conditions, 1/508 honest seats at 30% collusion, 8/492 valid seats, and n=756 near-miss seats) without an explicit unit derivation.

Table 1's caption (PDF p. 6) says outcomes are pooled over colluder shares 10-50%, but 'Valid released (of 96)' and 'Forged released (of 48)' include the 0% colluder share runs while only the 120-target denominator excludes 0%.

Figure 1's caption (PDF p. 7) claims to plot 'the committee regimes that were ever captured', but omits Committee 3-of-5 (captured 23 and 20 times in Table 1) from both Figure 1 and Table 3 (PDF p. 13).

Contribution 5 (PDF p. 2) claims 'complete logs', which is contradicted by Appendix D (PDF p. 15) listing missing full prompts, raw responses, git revisions, pinned temperatures, provider request IDs, and retry arrays.
Section 3.2 S2 (PDF p. 4) verifies immediate success of an eligible execution attempt rather than temporal liveness under fairness assumptions.

Section 3.4 (PDF p. 5) states that output caps were kept non-binding via retries, whereas Appendix C.3 and D (PDF pp. 13-15) note missing retry metadata for 30,096/32,832 records and Appendix B.3 (PDF pp. 12-13) shows the replacement run changed one 4-of-7 hidden capture from 1 to 0.

Code and Data (PDF p. 9) and the LLM Usage Statement (PDF p. 15) refer to a 2026-11-09 audit and correction without timezone-qualified submission timestamps relative to the Nov 8, 11:59 PM AoE deadline.

Section 3.4 (PDF p. 5) omits how 1-of-1, 2-of-3, and 3-of-5 committees are selected from the 7-seat draw, and Table 1 (PDF p. 6) pools visible-board runs (where auditors see the 50-agent tally) with hidden-board runs.
Global statements in the Abstract (PDF p. 1), Section 1 (PDF p. 2), Section 3.2 (PDF p. 4), and Section 5 (PDF p. 8) blur the depth/world bounds and the distinction between G1, G2, and G3.

revised_own_concerns.issue: The paper motivates the auditor committee by splitting 'what can be checked mechanically ... from what must be judged (is this release safe?)' (PDF p. 2-3, Section 1 & Section 3.1), yet the 12 invalid target cases in the benchmark ('build-only, wrong-artifact and wrong-run receipts', Section 3.4, PDF p. 4) and the near-miss cases ('two-character digest change or issuer capitalization', Section 4.3, PDF p. 7) are syntactic field mismatches on structured receipts that are mechanically decidable. Because the task reduces to exact field matching rather than ambiguous semantic judgment, honest LLM auditors make virtually zero errors (0/746 in main sweeps), leaving correlated honest errors (Knight & Leveson, 1986) under G3 empirically untested; moreover, the text never shows a concrete example distinguishing a worker receipt from an auditor attestation.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Explicitly scope the abstract, Section 3.1, Section 3.4, and Conclusion to state that this benchmark proxies judgment with structured receipt-field inspection to establish a clean ground-truth baseline, and add a compact worked example (or small table) showing an exact valid receipt, each invalid target rule, what the model sees in its prompt, and what the kernel checks mechanically.

revised_own_concerns.issue: In Figure 1 (PDF p. 7) and Table 3 (PDF p. 13), observed capture rates drop non-monotonically from 30% collusion (33.3% capture for DS 1-of-1) to 40% collusion (16.7% capture) because each colluder share uses a single seed (only 12 independent committee draws per share, 60 total across 10-50%), yet Figure 1 plots only the theoretical a-priori G3 curve and omits the realized G2 seat bound per share. In addition, Table 1's caption (PDF p. 6) states that outcomes are pooled over colluder shares 10-50% (which matches the 120 target trials), whereas the 96 valid and 48 forged trials actually pool across all six shares 0-50% (6 shares x 2 conditions x 8 valid or 4 forged cases).
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Plot the realized G2 seat-bound opportunity rate at each share on Figure 1 (and note draw-level uncertainty across the 12 independent draws per share), add the realized G2 seat bound count (out of 24) to every cell of Table 3, state the 60-independent-draw pairing directly in Table 1's main caption/headers, and clarify in Table 1's caption that Valid (96) and Forged (48) pool over 0-50% collusion while Targets (120) pool over 10-50%.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Several experimental controls and data-provenance boundaries in Section 3.4 (PDF pp. 4-5) need clearer qualification in the main text: (1) Section 3.4 does not specify the selection rule used to derive the 1-of-1, 2-of-3, and 3-of-5 committees from the single 7-seat draw, and Table 1/Figure 1 pool visible-board runs (where auditors see the 50-agent vote tally and comments before attesting) with hidden-board runs when evaluating 'standalone' committees; (2) the decisive gated-majority baseline is an offline reconstruction using fresh synthetic keys because original signing keys were not retained (Appendix D, PDF p. 15); and (3) Section 3.4 states unconditionally that output caps are kept non-binding via retries and Contribution 5 (PDF p. 2) claims 'complete logs', whereas Appendices B.3, C.3, and D (PDF pp. 12-15) disclose that 30,096/32,832 main records lack retry metadata, raw prompts/responses were not stored, and replacing the truncated DeepSeek 30% run changed 4-of-7 hidden capture from 1 to 0.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: In Section 3.4, clarify the exact seat-selection rule used to form 1-of-1, 2-of-3, and 3-of-5 from the 7-seat draw, report in Appendix C whether visible-board and hidden-board capture counts differ, explain why the synthetic-key reconstruction of gated majority is mechanically equivalent to live execution, replace 'complete logs' in Contribution 5 with 'structured decision logs', and qualify the non-binding output cap claim in Section 3.4 with the retry-metadata caveat and 1-to-0 replacement sensitivity from Appendix B.3.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Figure 1's caption (PDF p. 7) states that it plots 'the committee regimes that were ever captured', and Table 3 (PDF p. 13) tabulates unsafe releases by colluder share, but both omit 'Committee 3-of-5' even though Table 1 (PDF p. 6) shows Committee 3-of-5 was captured 23/120 times (DS) and 20/120 times (GPT). Furthermore, Section 4.3 (PDF p. 7) reports detector F1 of 0.97-1.0 across shares without a corresponding per-share precision/recall/F1 breakdown in Appendix B.4 or C.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a '3-of-5' column to Table 3, either add a fourth panel for Committee 3-of-5 to Figure 1 or revise Figure 1's caption to say 'selected committee regimes', and include a compact per-share precision/recall/F1 table for the public-log detector in Appendix B.4 or C.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Several citations and bibliography entries (PDF pp. 2, 3, 9, 10) are inconsistently formatted: (1) arXiv:2603.25100 is cited in-text and in the bibliography by a fragment of its title ('From Logic Monopoly, 2026') rather than its author(s); (2) SQLite is cited as '(SQLite)' with no year due to '\bibitem[SQLite()]{sqlite}'; (3) Hammond et al. (2025), Greenblatt et al. (2024), and Motwani et al. (2024) print literal 'et al.' in References while other multi-author entries list all authors; and (4) classic entries omit volume/page numbers and recent 2026 arXiv preprints should be verified for exact author/title metadata.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Replace 'From Logic Monopoly (2026)' with the verified author surname(s) of arXiv:2603.25100, add a verified year or 'n.d.' to the SQLite citation, standardize author lists and publication details in the bibliography, and verify all 2026 arXiv identifiers.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Two template and submission-requirement issues appear on PDF pp. 1, 9, and 10: (1) on the title page (PDF p. 1), the first author ('Alejandro Castellanos') has an empty affiliation field ('\authorcell{Alejandro Castellanos}{}') and 'With Apart Research' is ambiguous; and (2) counting the separate title page (PDF p. 1) plus the seven numbered body pages (PDF pp. 2-8) plus 'Code and Data' and 'Author Contributions' on PDF p. 9 places non-reference, non-appendix content at nine physical pages against the eight-page cap, while PDF p. 10 is left 80% blank after the last five references.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Add Alejandro Castellanos's affiliation (or 'Independent Researcher') on the title page, clarify Apart Research's role as hackathon organizer, move 'Code and Data' and 'Author Contributions' into an appendix (or fold the title page into page 1) so all non-reference/non-appendix pages fit strictly within 8 physical pages, and tighten bibliography spacing so References finish on page 8 without leaving PDF p. 10 mostly blank.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Layout, heading hierarchy, and table completeness have minor defects: (1) Section 5 (PDF p. 8) and Appendix A (PDF p. 11) use unnumbered '\subsection*' while Appendices B and C (PDF pp. 12-13) use bold run-in '\head{B.1 ...}' paragraphs; (2) B.2 ('B.2 Verification results. Table 2.') and C.2 ('C.2 Honest error on near-miss releases. Table 4.') consist of two-word sentence fragments; (3) Table 2 (PDF p. 12) omits explicit shortest-counterexample step counts for four of the seven mutants ('skip seat check', 'skip binding', 'count duplicates', 'skip audit'); and (4) Table 1 (PDF p. 6), Figure 1 (PDF p. 7), and Figure 2/Table 4 (PDF p. 14) split sentences across pages.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Use a consistent subsection hierarchy across Appendices A-D, replace the two-word fragments in B.2 and C.2 with complete sentences, fill in the shortest-counterexample step counts for all seven mutants in Table 2, and reposition floats to paragraph boundaries so they do not interrupt sentences mid-page.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Several terminology and prose choices slow down the reader: (1) the '2026-11-09' audit notes on PDF pp. 9 and 15 lack timezone-qualified timestamps relative to the Nov 8 AoE deadline and include superfluous AI-review score history ('round 1 ended with three weak rejects and one reject'); (2) S2 in Section 3.2 (PDF p. 4) is called 'liveness' when it checks immediate step-level execution success, Finding 3 (PDF p. 6) uses 'liveness' to mean valid-release availability, and global phrases ('every reachable state', singular 'the guarantee') blur G1-G3; (3) Section 4.3 (PDF p. 7) shifts between multiple denominators (0/746, 2/108, 1/508, 8/492, and n=756 in Table 4) without deriving the units; and (4) acronyms (MCP, A2A, HMAC, TF-IDF) are not expanded at first use and Section 3.4's sentence on excluding non-reasoning models (PDF p. 5) is logically convoluted.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Provide timezone-qualified timestamps for the pre-deadline submission vs. post-audit corrections while trimming the superfluous AI-review round tally, distinguish step-level execution enabledness (S2) and empirical valid-release acceptance from formal temporal liveness, name G1/G2/G3 explicitly with depth bounds, derive the denominator units in Section 4.3 (e.g., 108 case-conditions = 6 zero-collusion near-miss runs x 18 invalid cases, 756 auditor slots = 108 x 7 seats), expand acronyms on first use, and simplify the reasoning-model sentence in Section 3.4.

rebuttals.response: We agree that the manuscript does not confirm whether smaller committees take the first m seats or use another subsetting rule, and we have updated our C3 fix to ask the authors to clarify the exact selection rule.

We agree that preserving timezone-qualified timestamps for the 2026-11-09 audit is important for verifying AoE deadline compliance, and have refined C8 to retain the dated provenance changelog while removing only the superfluous automated-review round tally.
